html:
SMTO-TSK-0028 — Manage this task from its own conversation

GUID: c4b2e770-ad23-4510-ab9a-e96b0e2bdbeb
Slug: task-lane-endpoint-required
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • This task is waiting in a conversation's task list, so it can only be changed from that conversation. SMTO didn't change it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page, then open the conversation where you sent this message. An old browser tab can reach the task in an outdated way that SMTO no longer accepts.
  2. Use the task's own buttons in that conversation, or the Queued list there, to edit, reorder or delete it. Waiting tasks keep their saved settings and can only be changed from their conversation.
  3. If a script or another tool made this request, have it send chat tasks through the conversation task queue instead. The general task list and older connections can't create, reconnect or archive conversation tasks.

What success looks like

  • The task appears in its conversation with its normal buttons, and your change takes effect.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't send the same message again as a new task; the original is still saved in its conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A durable conversation (chat) task was created, reconnected, submitted or archived through a general task route instead of its conversation-lane endpoints and complete composer snapshot.

What this means

  • A durable queued chat task is submitted, archived or created through a legacy/general route that lacks its lane-owned immutable snapshot and controls. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • A durable queued chat task is submitted, archived or created through a legacy/general route that lacks its lane-owned immutable snapshot and controls.

How to diagnose it

  • Check whether the request belongs to a durable chat lane and use its existing binding.

How to fix it

  • Use the conversation-lane API (/api/agent/conversation-tasks and the lane's run-next, reorder and delete controls) with a complete composer snapshot instead of /api/agent/tasks, a direct native request submit, or task archive. Reconnect to an existing chat task through its lane binding rather than resubmitting the request.
  • Reconnect to the owning conversation and use its task lane controls. Submit new composer tasks through the supported conversation task flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The task is addressed through the owning lane's supported admission or management route.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
